threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You walk into a pub and order a ‘pint’ without knowing you’re supposed to ask for a ‘lager’ or ‘bitter’ first. Instant giveaway.
Saw a guy on the 77 last night trying to pay with a half-eaten apple. The driver just stared, so he switched to a crumpled fiver. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled upon a random street festival—music blasting, food stalls from every culture, and everyone just vibing together.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a currywurst at 3 AM after a night out, while a street musician plays techno on the corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name the exact taco truck that shuts down during BART delays, while newcomers are still just waiting for the N-Judah.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a tourist mistaking the Muni driver for an Uber. The driver just laughed, pointing to the sign. Classic Tenderloin confusion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals hit up the plaça on weekends. Most of us avoid it like the plague—way too many selfie sticks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the subway machines—always tapping their cards but missing the simple fact that you need to scan it on the way out.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still believe the bus will come on time. Watch the locals flinch at the first 'expected arrival'.
Caught a natter between two guys on the 45 last night. One swore he saw a ghost at the old cinema. Brixton’s stories never sleep.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: You know you’re in Neukölln when the café on the corner runs out of croissants because the baker’s cat decided to nap on the delivery truck.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a Späti selling vegan döner that doubles as an art gallery after dark. Totally unique vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they still grumble about the BART delays like it’s a rite of passage, not just another commute hassle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy pull out a full-size piano on the corner of Eddy and Jones, played a magical tune as the 19 bus rolled by. Only in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals use them to catch up over vermut and tapas, not just for the scenery.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order a café con leche—only the locals know it’s a morning drink, not an afternoon treat.
